title: Quincy Jones's Dinah Washington date
summary: Crawford repeats that Quincy Jones hired him and Milt Hinton for a Dinah Washington date because he wanted drummers who just play.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Well, because I know Quincy Jones spoke highly of you, and I was wondering, did you feel a relief from, say, the monotony of working in the shows, when you got a chance to do a date where you got to play with musicians that didn't play the same thing all the time?

Well, about that, Quincy Jones was nice enough to call me. Also, he called Milt Hinton on bass, the date was Dinah Washington record date. And so Quincy was very, very pleased with the work we did, because he said the drumming situation today is completely out of hand. He wants some guys that play, just play. And Dinah did Lady D or something, I can't recall. I have the records here somewhere.
